post_Santo_to_NC_reset.rule: recompute actual MR and crew-quality after Santo sorties. Do not reset to 143. Reserve-deck substitutions are replacements, not free additions.

the same 6-7 D-day boats cannot remain at full forward effectiveness indefinitely. Center immediate post-Santo useful line 4-6; after replenishment/rotation, 5-7 for NC if no losses. Any >7 NC line requires a newly named hull allocation audit.
fuel, torpedoes, bombardment ammunition, maintenance days and floatplane losses carry forward; Hiei/Arashi release can offset some attrition only after their gates.
post-landing ledger becomes physical survivors + repaired vehicles. Branch 24-72h return improves repairable returns but never restores destroyed/drowned/abandoned machines.

15th Independent Engineer elements used to make Santo usable cannot simultaneously be counted in the NC first wave. Release to NC only after Santo minimum runway/port/garrison tasks are explicitly handed over.

Kawaguchi main body remains the principal NC follow-on reserve. Its own vehicle/artillery/shipping wallet must be closed at the actual NC decision date; do not copy the Santo hardware package onto it.
NC defender/air/naval state must be re-audited at the actual post-Santo date. Delay is not free: New Caledonia receives additional air/ground preparation while Japan repairs and builds forward bases.

attrition_feedback: Loss of veteran carrier strike leaders/navigators/maintenance nuclei matters more than the same count of replacement aircraft; track separately.
Loss/suppression of Shortland/Rekata/Tulagi reduces search/recontact redundancy and forces carrier/shipboard aircraft to spend more sorties on ISR.
A captured Santo base lowers carrier ISR/fixed-target burden only after its conditional air/water-aviation gates pass.
Fuel/oiler damage can nullify nominally available hull additions; capability clock never bypasses logistics.
